overview: This House resolution, known as a 'rule,' sets the terms for House debate on four bills. H.R. 2483 would renew federal programs for preventing and treating opioid addiction and supporting recovery; it gets one hour of general debate and a limited set of amendments chosen in advance by the Rules Committee. The other three concern the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that helps small businesses: H.R. 2931 would move certain SBA offices out of 'sanctuary' cities that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, H.R. 2966 would require loan applicants to provide proof of citizenship status, and H.R. 2987 would cap the number of small business lending companies. Each of those three gets one hour of debate and no amendments. The House adopted it on June 4, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule moves bills on the opioid crisis and small business lending to the floor in an orderly way, with time for debate and some amendments on the opioid bill.
against: Critics say the rule blocks amendments on the three small business bills and bundles unrelated measures together, limiting members' chances to change them.
